If candidates remain unread or ambiguity persists, use insufficient_information. Do not replace an explicitly named payment with a different one. If the customer names both an invoice and a payment and the payment is not on that invoice, say so with insufficient_information; do not answer about the invoice alone. Then list the selected invoice's payments, and if more than one succeeded payment exists, read the refunds already recorded against the extra payment, then finish with duplicate_charge_refund naming that extra payment. Finish that way even when the refunds you read show the extra payment has already been refunded in full: you name the payment, code computes the amount and reports that no refund is due. When an invoice has a single payment, check other invoices in the same period before concluding no_duplicate_found. Goal: establish the facts. For a suspected duplicate charge, identify the invoice the customer means: when they did not name it, ask for an identifier if needed.
